section_1.title: The Mystery of Primes: Meet the Detective
section_1.content: Introduce a character, 'Detective Prime,' who is trying to find a pattern in the chaotic distribution of prime numbers (2, 3, 5, 7, 11...). Explain that while primes seem random, the Riemann zeta function is the 'secret map' that describes their behavior. Use a visual of a scattered field of stars representing primes that slowly align into a grid.
section_1.example: Imagine Detective Prime looking at a series of houses (numbers); only some are 'golden' (primes). He needs a single formula to predict where the next golden house will be.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Power of Infinite Sums
section_2.content: Before the main function, explain the concept of an infinite series. Use a visual of a 'Zeno's Paradox' walker moving toward a wall: 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8... showing that an infinite number of steps can result in a finite distance (2). Contrast this with the Harmonic Series (1 + 1/2 + 1/3...) which grows forever to infinity.
section_2.example: An ant walking half the remaining distance to a crumb every second—it gets closer and closer but represents a convergent sum.

section_3.title: Defining the Zeta Function
section_3.content: Introduce the formal definition: ζ(s) = ∑ (1/n^s) for n=1 to ∞. Show the formula clearly. Use an animation where 's' is a slider. When s=1, the sum explodes (Harmonic Series). When s=2, it settles. Show the numbers 1/1^s, 1/2^s, 1/3^s as shrinking squares on a balance scale.
section_3.example: If s=2, the sum is 1 + 1/4 + 1/9 + 1/16... This is the famous 'Basel Problem' solved by Euler.

section_4.title: The Euler Product: The Prime Connection
section_4.content: Present the 'Magic Bridge.' Show the Zeta function on one side (a sum of all integers) and the Euler Product on the other (a product involving only primes). Use an animation of 'Prime Gears' turning to produce the entire sequence of natural numbers. This establishes why the zeta function is the key to prime number theory.
section_4.example: Visualize a 'Sieve of Eratosthenes' machine where the Zeta function acts as the fuel, and the output is the list of prime numbers.

section_5.title: Entering the Complex Realm (Analytic Continuation)
section_5.content: Transition from real numbers to the complex plane (s = σ + it). Use a 3D 'topographical map' animation. The 'floor' is the complex plane, and the 'height' is the value of |ζ(s)|. Show the function 'stretching' beyond its original domain to cover the entire map, creating mountains and valleys.
section_5.example: Imagine a stretchy rubber sheet that initially only covers the right side of a table; analytic continuation is the process of pulling that sheet to cover the whole table without tearing it.

section_6.title: The Riemann Hypothesis: The Critical Line
section_6.content: Identify the 'valleys' (zeros) of the function. Highlight the 'Critical Strip' between 0 and 1. Show the 'Critical Line' at x = 0.5. Explain that Riemann's billion-dollar guess is that all 'non-trivial' zeros lie exactly on this line. Use an animation of a tightrope walker (the function's zeros) perfectly balanced on this 0.5 line.
section_6.example: If a single zero is found off this line, the 'Prime Detective's' map is wrong, and the music of the primes would turn into noise.

section_7.title: Summary and Real-World Impact
section_7.content: Conclude with the importance of the function in modern cryptography and quantum physics. Recap the journey from a simple sum to the complex landscape of primes. Show a digital shield (encryption) being powered by the stability of the Riemann Hypothesis.
section_7.example: The security of your online bank password relies on the fact that primes are hard to predict—a secret held by the Zeta function.

section_1.title: The Mystery of Primes: Meet the Detective
section_1.content: Introduce a character, 'Detective Prime,' who is trying to find a pattern in the chaotic distribution of prime numbers (2, 3, 5, 7, 11...). Explain that while primes seem random, the Riemann zeta function is the 'secret map' that describes their behavior. Use a visual of a scattered field of stars representing primes that slowly align into a grid.
section_1.example: Imagine Detective Prime looking at a series of houses (numbers); only some are 'golden' (primes). He needs a single formula to predict where the next golden house will be.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Power of Infinite Sums
section_2.content: Before the main function, explain the concept of an infinite series. Use a visual of a 'Zeno's Paradox' walker moving toward a wall: 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8... showing that an infinite number of steps can result in a finite distance (2). Contrast this with the Harmonic Series (1 + 1/2 + 1/3...) which grows forever to infinity.
section_2.example: An ant walking half the remaining distance to a crumb every second—it gets closer and closer but represents a convergent sum.

section_3.title: Defining the Zeta Function
section_3.content: Introduce the formal definition: ζ(s) = ∑ (1/n^s) for n=1 to ∞. Show the formula clearly. Use an animation where 's' is a slider. When s=1, the sum explodes (Harmonic Series). When s=2, it settles. Show the numbers 1/1^s, 1/2^s, 1/3^s as shrinking squares on a balance scale.
section_3.example: If s=2, the sum is 1 + 1/4 + 1/9 + 1/16... This is the famous 'Basel Problem' solved by Euler.

section_4.title: The Euler Product: The Prime Connection
section_4.content: Present the 'Magic Bridge.' Show the Zeta function on one side (a sum of all integers) and the Euler Product on the other (a product involving only primes). Use an animation of 'Prime Gears' turning to produce the entire sequence of natural numbers. This establishes why the zeta function is the key to prime number theory.
section_4.example: Visualize a 'Sieve of Eratosthenes' machine where the Zeta function acts as the fuel, and the output is the list of prime numbers.

section_5.title: Entering the Complex Realm (Analytic Continuation)
section_5.content: Transition from real numbers to the complex plane (s = σ + it). Use a 3D 'topographical map' animation. The 'floor' is the complex plane, and the 'height' is the value of |ζ(s)|. Show the function 'stretching' beyond its original domain to cover the entire map, creating mountains and valleys.
section_5.example: Imagine a stretchy rubber sheet that initially only covers the right side of a table; analytic continuation is the process of pulling that sheet to cover the whole table without tearing it.

section_6.title: The Riemann Hypothesis: The Critical Line
section_6.content: Identify the 'valleys' (zeros) of the function. Highlight the 'Critical Strip' between 0 and 1. Show the 'Critical Line' at x = 0.5. Explain that Riemann's billion-dollar guess is that all 'non-trivial' zeros lie exactly on this line. Use an animation of a tightrope walker (the function's zeros) perfectly balanced on this 0.5 line.
section_6.example: If a single zero is found off this line, the 'Prime Detective's' map is wrong, and the music of the primes would turn into noise.

section_7.title: Summary and Real-World Impact
section_7.content: Conclude with the importance of the function in modern cryptography and quantum physics. Recap the journey from a simple sum to the complex landscape of primes. Show a digital shield (encryption) being powered by the stability of the Riemann Hypothesis.
section_7.example: The security of your online bank password relies on the fact that primes are hard to predict—a secret held by the Zeta function.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Euler Product: The Prime Connection",
            [
                "The zeta function transforms into a product over primes.",
                "Animated gears represent primes building every single natural number.",
                "This bridge links basic counting to the depth of primes."
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        COLOR_ZETA = "#58C4DD"
        COLOR_EULER = "#83C167"
        COLOR_PRIME = "#FF8080"
        COLOR_NATURAL = "#F0E442"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # The zeta function transforms into a product over primes.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_ZETA)
        
        zeta_sum = MathTex(r"\zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^s}", color=COLOR_ZETA)
        euler_prod = MathTex(r"\prod_{p \in \text{Primes}} \frac{1}{1-p^{-s}}", color=COLOR_EULER)
        equals = MathTex("=", color=WHITE)

        formula_group = VGroup(zeta_sum, equals, euler_prod).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(formula_group, "B1", "C6", scale_factor=0.9)

        self.play(Write(zeta_sum))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(Write(equals), Write(euler_prod))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animated gears represent primes building every single natural number.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_PRIME)

        def create_gear(radius, teeth_count, color):
            gear = Circle(radius=radius, color=color, fill_opacity=0.3)
            teeth = VGroup()
            for i in range(teeth_count):
                tooth = Rectangle(width=0.2, height=0.1, color=color, fill_opacity=1)
                angle = i * (360 / teeth_count) * DEGREES
                tooth.rotate(angle)
                tooth.move_to(gear.get_center() + np.array([radius * np.cos(angle), radius * np.sin(angle), 0]))
                teeth.add(tooth)
            return VGroup(gear, teeth)

        gear_primes = [2, 3, 5, 7]
        gears = VGroup()
        gear_labels = VGroup()
        
        positions = ["E1", "E2", "E3", "E4"]
        for i, p in enumerate(gear_primes):
            g = create_gear(0.3, 8, COLOR_PRIME)
            self.place_at_grid(g, positions[i])
            lbl = MathTex(str(p), font_size=24, color=WHITE)
            lbl.move_to(g.get_center())
            gears.add(g)
            gear_labels.add(lbl)

        # Value tracker for rotation
        rotation_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        for i, g in enumerate(gears):
            # Alternate rotation direction
            direction = 1 if i % 2 == 0 else -1
            g.add_updater(lambda mob, dt, d=direction: mob.rotate(d * 0.5 * dt))

        self.play(Create(gears), Write(gear_labels))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # This bridge links basic counting to the depth of primes.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_NATURAL)

        # Flow of natural numbers
        def create_natural_flow():
            numbers = VGroup()
            for n in range(1, 11):
                num = MathTex(str(n), color=COLOR_NATURAL, font_size=32)
                numbers.add(num)
            return numbers

        flowing_numbers = create_natural_flow()
        
        # Start point is near the last gear (E4), end point is off-screen right (E6 area)
        start_pos = self.grid["E4"] + RIGHT * 0.8
        end_pos = self.grid["E6"] + RIGHT * 1.5

        def animate_number(num, delay):
            num.move_to(start_pos)
            num.set_opacity(0)
            self.add(num)
            self.play(
                num.animate.move_to(end_pos).set_opacity(1),
                run_time=2,
                rate_func=linear,
                delay=delay
            )
            self.play(FadeOut(num, run_time=0.5))

        # We'll use a simpler sequential animation for the numbers to ensure reliability
        for i, num in enumerate(flowing_numbers[:6]):
            num.move_to(start_pos)
            self.play(
                num.animate.move_to(end_pos).set_opacity(0),
                run_time=1.5,
                rate_func=linear
            )
            # Remove from scene after animation to save performance
            self.remove(num)

        self.wait(2)

            "The zeta function sums one over n to power s.",

            "As s increases, the sum settles into finite values.",
            "For s equals two, we solve the famous Basel Problem.",
            "The function converges for all values greater than one."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # The formal definition ζ(s) = ∑ (1/n^s) for n=1 to ∞ appears in the center in white (#FFFFFF).
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        zeta_formula = MathTex(r"\zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^s}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(zeta_formula, 'A1', 'B6', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(zeta_formula))

        s_val_text.next_to(slider_label, RIGHT)
        
        slider_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        slider_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(slider_line.n2p(s_tracker.get_value())))

            s_val = s_tracker.get_value()
            curr_y = base_pos[1]
            for i, r in enumerate(m):
                n = i + 1
                h = 2.0 / (n**s_val)
                r.set_height(h, stretch=True)
                r.move_to([base_pos[0], curr_y + h/2, 0])
                curr_y += h

        # Squares for left plate (ζ(2))

        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.05, aligned_edge=DOWN).scale(0.4)
        
        # Result for right plate
        basel_res_plate = MathTex(r"\frac{\pi^2}{6}", color="#FFD700").scale(0.7)
        
        # Assemble Scale relative positions

I have completed the Manim code for **Section 3: Defining the Zeta Function**.

### Key Features:
- **Formula Presentation**: Displays $\zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^s}$ in the top section of the grid.
- **Dynamic Slider**: Implements a `ValueTracker`-based slider for $s$ that controls the subsequent animations.
- **Tower Animation**: At $s=1$, a tower of rectangles represents the diverging Harmonic series. As $s$ increases to 2, the tower height settles.
- **Basel Problem Visualization**: Transitions to a balance scale showing the sum of squares $1/n^2$ balancing with the result $\frac{\pi^2}{6}$ in gold.
- **Convergence Domain**: Highlights the domain $s > 1$ with a green box in the top-right corner.
- **Grid Compliance**: All elements are strictly positioned using the `place_at_grid` and `place_in_area` methods on the 6x6 grid (A1-F6).

The code is optimized for performance by using updaters to modify existing mobjects rather than regenerating them with `always_redraw`.

```python
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Zeta Function", [
            "The zeta function sums one over n to power s.",
            "At s equals one, the harmonic series explodes infinitely.",
            "As s increases, the sum settles into finite values.",
            "For s equals two, we solve the famous Basel Problem.",
            "The function converges for all values greater than one."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        zeta_formula = MathTex(r"\zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^s}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(zeta_formula, 'A1', 'B6', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(zeta_formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE_B))
        
        s_tracker = ValueTracker(2.0)
        
        # Slider setup
        slider_line = NumberLine(x_range=[1, 4, 1], length=3, include_tip=True, color=GRAY)
        slider_label = MathTex("s =", font_size=24).next_to(slider_line, LEFT)
        s_val_text = DecimalNumber(s_tracker.get_value(), num_decimal_places=1, font_size=24)
        s_val_text.add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(s_tracker.get_value()))
        s_val_text.next_to(slider_label, RIGHT)
        
        slider_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        slider_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(slider_line.n2p(s_tracker.get_value())))
        
        slider_group = VGroup(slider_line, slider_label, s_val_text, slider_dot)
        self.place_at_grid(slider_group, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        base_pos = self.grid['F3']
        rects = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=0.4, height=0.1, fill_opacity=0.8, color=BLUE_B) for _ in range(12)])
        
        def update_tower(m):
            s_val = s_tracker.get_value()
            curr_y = base_pos[1]
            for i, r in enumerate(m):
                n = i + 1
                h = 2.0 / (n**s_val)
                r.set_height(h, stretch=True)
                r.move_to([base_pos[0], curr_y + h/2, 0])
                curr_y += h
                
        rects.add_updater(update_tower)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(slider_group), FadeIn(rects))
        self.play(s_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(CYAN))
        self.play(s_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        rects.clear_updaters()
        self.play(FadeOut(slider_group), FadeOut(rects))
        
        pivot = Triangle(color=GRAY).scale(0.15)
        beam = Line(LEFT*1.5, RIGHT*1.5, color=GRAY)
        left_plate = Line(LEFT*0.6, RIGHT*0.6, color=GRAY)
        right_plate = Line(LEFT*0.6, RIGHT*0.6, color=GRAY)
        
        squares = VGroup(*[
            Square(side_length=1.2/(n**1), fill_opacity=0.6, color=CYAN) 
            for n in range(1, 6)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.05, aligned_edge=DOWN).scale(0.4)
        
        basel_res_plate = MathTex(r"\frac{\pi^2}{6}", color="#FFD700").scale(0.7)
        
        beam.next_to(pivot, UP, buff=0)
        left_plate.move_to(beam.get_start() + UP*0.1)
        right_plate.move_to(beam.get_end() + UP*0.1)
        squares.next_to(left_plate, UP, buff=0)
        basel_res_plate.next_to(right_plate, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        scale_group = VGroup(pivot, beam, left_plate, right_plate, squares, basel_res_plate)
        self.place_in_area(scale_group, 'D1', 'F5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(scale_group))
        
        basel_full = MathTex(r"\zeta(2) = \frac{\pi^2}{6}", color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(basel_full, 'E6', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(basel_full))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#90EE90"))
        conv_text = Text("Convergence: s > 1", font_size=20, color="#90EE90")
        conv_box = SurroundingRectangle(conv_text, color="#90EE90", buff=0.1)
        conv_group = VGroup(conv_box, conv_text)
        self.place_at_grid(conv_group, 'A6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(conv_group))
        self.wait(2)
```

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        title = "The Mystery of Primes: Meet the Detective"
        lines = [
            "Prime numbers appear scattered and random across the field.",
            "Meet Detective Prime, searching for patterns in their distribution.",
            "The Riemann zeta function reveals their hidden, secret map."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        for r in rows:
            for c in cols:

        for i, dot in enumerate(dots):

            run_time=3
        )

    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title = "Defining the Zeta Function"
        lines = [
            "The zeta function sums one over n to power s.",
            "At s equals one, the harmonic series explodes infinitely.",
            "As s increases, the sum settles into finite values.",
            "For s equals two, we solve the famous Basel Problem.",
            "The function converges for all values greater than one."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Asset Paths
        tower_path = "/mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tower.svg"
        scale_path = "/mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/scale.svg"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        formula = Text("ζ(s) = ∑ 1/n^s", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=1.1)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        l2_color = BLUE_A
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(l2_color))
        
        s_tracker = ValueTracker(2.0)
        
        # Slider UI - Added label_constructor=Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        slider_line = NumberLine(x_range=[1, 4, 1], length=2.4, include_numbers=True, font_size=16, label_constructor=Text)
        self.place_at_grid(slider_line, "C3", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        s_label = Text("s = ", font_size=24)
        # Added mob_class=Text to DecimalNumber to avoid LaTeX dependency
        s_val_disp = DecimalNumber(s_tracker.get_value(), num_decimal_places=1, font_size=24, mob_class=Text)
        s_val_disp.add_updater(lambda d: d.set_value(s_tracker.get_value()))
        slider_ctrl = VGroup(s_label, s_val_disp).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1).next_to(slider_line, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        slider_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW, radius=0.08)
        slider_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(slider_line.n2p(s_tracker.get_value())))
        
        # Tower Visual (Asset)
        tower_icon = SVGMobject(tower_path).set_color(BLUE_E).set_opacity(0.2)
        self.place_in_area(tower_icon, "D1", "F3", scale_factor=1.3)
        
        # Dynamic Blocks
        blocks = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=0.4, height=0.1, fill_opacity=0.8, color=l2_color, stroke_width=1) for _ in range(5)])
        
        def update_blocks(m):
            s_val = s_tracker.get_value()
            base_point = tower_icon.get_bottom()
            center_x = base_point[0]
            curr_y = base_point[1]
            for i, b in enumerate(m):
                n = i + 1
                h = 1.3 / (n**s_val)
                b.stretch_to_fit_height(max(h, 0.02))
                b.move_to([center_x, curr_y + b.get_height()/2, 0])
                curr_y += b.get_height()
        
        blocks.add_updater(update_blocks)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(slider_line), FadeIn(slider_ctrl), FadeIn(slider_dot))
        self.play(FadeIn(tower_icon), FadeIn(blocks))
        
        # Animate to Harmonic Series (s=1)
        self.play(s_tracker.animate.set_value(1.0), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        l3_color = TEAL
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(l3_color))
        # Converging to higher s
        self.play(s_tracker.animate.set_value(3.0), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        l4_color = "#FFD700" # Gold
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(l4_color))
        
        # Return to s=2 for Basel visual as implied by storyboard
        self.play(s_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=0.8)
        self.play(FadeOut(slider_line, slider_ctrl, slider_dot, tower_icon, blocks), run_time=0.5)
        
        # Balance Scale (Asset)
        scale_icon = SVGMobject(scale_path).set_color(GRAY)
        self.place_in_area(scale_icon, "D2", "F5", scale_factor=1.4)
        
        # Basel Squares
        basel_sqs = VGroup(*[
            Square(side_length=0.6/(n), fill_opacity=0.7, color=TEAL)
            for n in range(1, 5)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.05, aligned_edge=DOWN)
        basel_sqs.move_to(scale_icon.get_center() + LEFT * 1.0 + UP * 0.45)
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        basel_result = Text("ζ(2) = π²/6", font_size=32, color=l4_color)
        self.place_at_grid(basel_result, "E6", scale_factor=1.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(scale_icon), FadeIn(basel_sqs))
        self.play(Write(basel_result))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        l5_color = "#90EE90" # Light Green
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(l5_color))
        
        conv_text = Text("Convergence: s > 1", font_size=22, color=l5_color)
        conv_box = SurroundingRectangle(conv_text, color=l5_color, buff=0.2)
        conv_label = VGroup(conv_box, conv_text)
        self.place_at_grid(conv_label, "A6", scale_factor=1.0)

        ]
        self.setup_layout("Entering the Complex Realm (Analytic Continuation)", lecture_lines)

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])

class Section7Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title = "Summary and Real-World Impact"
        lines = [
            "- We compress these complex insights into a single core.",
            "- This math powers the security of our digital world.",
            "- Thus, the music of primes plays in perfect harmony."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Color definitions for matching
        COLOR_CORE = YELLOW
        COLOR_SHIELD = BLUE_B
        COLOR_FINAL = "#90EE90"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A montage of the prime grid, Euler gears, and the critical line shrinks into a central glowing core.
        
        # 1. Prime grid (montage component)
        prime_grid = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.06, color=BLUE_A) for _ in range(9)])
        prime_grid.arrange_in_grid(rows=3, cols=3, buff=0.2)
        self.place_at_grid(prime_grid, 'B2', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # 2. Euler gear (montage component)
        gear_base = Circle(radius=0.4, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        teeth = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(width=0.1, height=0.1, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
            .move_to([0.4 * np.cos(a), 0.4 * np.sin(a), 0])
            .rotate(a) 
            for a in np.linspace(0, 2*PI, 8, endpoint=False)
        ])
        gear = VGroup(gear_base, teeth)
        self.place_at_grid(gear, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # 3. Critical line (montage component)
        critical_line = Line(UP, DOWN, color=RED).scale(1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(critical_line, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        montage = VGroup(prime_grid, gear, critical_line)
        
        # 4. Central Glowing Core (target of transformation)
        core_center = Dot(radius=0.15, color=COLOR_CORE)
        core_halo = Circle(radius=0.3, color=COLOR_CORE, stroke_opacity=0.4).set_fill(COLOR_CORE, opacity=0.2)
        glowing_core = VGroup(core_center, core_halo)
        self.place_in_area(glowing_core, 'C3', 'D4', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Step 1: Animation
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_CORE)
        self.play(Create(montage), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(montage, glowing_core), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # A digital shield icon labeled 'Encryption' appears, powered by energy pulses from the central core.
        
        # Step 2: Highlight line and create shield
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_SHIELD)
        
        shield_points = [
            [0, 1.2, 0], [1, 0.8, 0], [1, -0.4, 0], [0, -1.3, 0], [-1, -0.4, 0], [-1, 0.8, 0], [0, 1.2, 0]
        ]
        shield_shape = VMobject().set_points_as_corners(shield_points)
        shield_shape.set_color(COLOR_SHIELD).set_fill(COLOR_SHIELD, opacity=0.25)
        shield_label = Text("Encryption", font_size=16, color=WHITE).move_to(shield_shape.get_center() + DOWN * 0.1)
        shield_group = VGroup(shield_shape, shield_label)
        self.place_in_area(shield_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(shield_group, scale=0.5))
        
        # energy pulses from central core
        for _ in range(3):
            pulse = Circle(radius=0.1, color=COLOR_CORE, stroke_width=3)
            pulse.move_to(glowing_core.get_center())
            self.add(pulse)
            self.play(
                pulse.animate.scale(12).set_stroke(opacity=0),
                run_time=0.9,
                rate_func=linear
            )
            self.remove(pulse)
            
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The screen fades to black with the final text 'The Music of Primes' appearing in soft green (#90EE90).
        
        # Step 3: Highlight line and final transition
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_FINAL)
        
        final_text = Text("The Music of Primes", font_size=42, color=COLOR_FINAL)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(self.lecture),
            FadeOut(self.title),
            FadeOut(shield_group),
            FadeOut(glowing_core),
            Write(final_text.move_to(ORIGIN)),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        title = "The Mystery of Primes: Meet the Detective"
        lines = [
            "Prime numbers appear scattered and random across the field.",
            "Meet Detective Prime, searching for patterns in their distribution.",
            "The Riemann zeta function reveals their hidden, secret map."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a field of scattered white dots representing primes
        # We use fixed random positions within the grid area B2-E5 to simulate "randomness"
        np.random.seed(42)
        dot_positions = []
        for _ in range(15):
            # Generating random offsets within the grid area
            rx = np.random.uniform(1.0, 5.0)
            ry = np.random.uniform(-1.8, 1.2)
            dot_positions.append(np.array([rx, ry, 0]))
            
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(pos, color=WHITE, radius=0.08) for pos in dot_positions])
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dots, lag_ratio=0.1), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Create Detective Prime icon (Simple circle and line for magnifying glass)
        detective_body = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#87CEEB", fill_opacity=0.8)
        magnifier_rim = Circle(radius=0.1, color=WHITE).shift(RIGHT*0.2 + DOWN*0.1)
        magnifier_handle = Line(magnifier_rim.get_bottom(), magnifier_rim.get_bottom() + DOWN*0.1 + RIGHT*0.1, color=WHITE)
        detective = VGroup(detective_body, magnifier_rim, magnifier_handle)
        
        # Initial position off-screen left (near grid A1/B1 but outside)
        detective.move_to(self.grid["B1"] + LEFT * 2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(detective))
        
        # Path for detective to scan the field
        scan_points = [self.grid["B2"], self.grid["D3"], self.grid["C5"], self.grid["E4"]]
        for point in scan_points:
            self.play(detective.animate.move_to(point), run_time=1.5, rate_func=smooth)
            self.wait(0.2)

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Create the gold formula ζ(s)
        zeta_formula = Text("ζ(s)", color="#FFD700", font_size=60)
        self.place_at_grid(zeta_formula, "A3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Define grid alignment positions (from B2 to E5)
        grid_spots = []
        rows = ["B", "C", "D", "E"]
        cols = ["2", "3", "4", "5"]
        for r in rows:
            for c in cols:
                grid_spots.append(self.grid[f"{r}{c}"])
        
        # Animate dots moving to grid and formula fading in
        dot_animations = []
        for i, dot in enumerate(dots):
            if i < len(grid_spots):
                dot_animations.append(dot.animate.move_to(grid_spots[i]))
            else:
                dot_animations.append(FadeOut(dot))

        self.play(
            FadeIn(zeta_formula, shift=UP),
            *dot_animations,
            detective.animate.scale(0.8).move_to(self.grid["F1"]),
            run_time=3
        )
        
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Final cleanup for the section
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

```python
        lecture_lines = [
            "- The zeta function transforms into a product over primes.",

        self.place_at_grid(euler_prod, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)

        for p, pos in zip(prime_values, grid_positions):
            # Load SVG and add a numeric label
            gear = SVGMobject(gear_path, color=color_line2, height=0.8)
            label = Text(str(p), font_size=18, color=WHITE)
            gear_unit = VGroup(gear, label)
            self.place_at_grid(gear_unit, pos, scale_factor=0.9)
            gears.add(gear_unit)

        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(g) for g in gears], lag_ratio=0.3))
        
        # Continuous rotation for gears
        for i, gear_unit in enumerate(gears):
            direction = 1 if i % 2 == 0 else -1
            gear_unit[0].add_updater(lambda m, dt, d=direction: m.rotate(d * dt * 0.5))

        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_line3))

        # Natural numbers flow out from the spinning prime gears
        numbers = VGroup()

            num = Text(str(i), font_size=24, color=color_line3)
            self.place_at_grid(num, "E1", scale_factor=1.0)
            numbers.add(num)

        flow_anims = []
        for i, num in enumerate(numbers):
            # Move from gears towards the right edge
            dest = self.grid["F6"] + RIGHT * (i * 0.4)
            flow_anims.append(num.animate(run_time=2, rate_func=linear).move_to(dest).set_opacity(0))

        self.play(LaggedStart(*flow_anims, lag_ratio=0.2))
        self.wait(2)

        # Cleanup updaters
        for gear_unit in gears:
            gear_unit[0].clear_updaters()
        
        # Final transition
        self.play(
            FadeOut(zeta_sum),
            FadeOut(euler_prod),
            FadeOut(gears),
            FadeOut(self.title),
            FadeOut(self.lecture)
        )
```

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout
        title_text = "Prerequisite: The Power of Infinite Sums"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Infinite steps can lead to a finite, definite distance.",
            "- Imagine walking halfway to a destination every single second.",
            "- Some series converge, while the harmonic series grows forever."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Assets and Colors
        walker_path = "/mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/walker.svg"
        COLOR_CONV = "#ADD8E6"
        COLOR_DIV = "#FF4500"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A number line from 0 to 2 appears; a walker [Asset: ...] moves in increments of 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        number_line = NumberLine(
            x_range=[0, 2.1, 0.5],
            length=5,
            include_numbers=True,
            font_size=20,
            color=WHITE
        )
        wall = Line(UP*0.4, DOWN*0.4, color=GREY, stroke_width=4).move_to(number_line.number_to_point(2))
        plane_group = VGroup(number_line, wall)
        
        # Fix Issue 32: Utilizing right-side space by placing plane_group in defined area.
        self.place_in_area(plane_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.3)
        
        walker = SVGMobject(walker_path)
        # Fix Issue 34: Defining indicator anchor at C4, then positioning at line start.
        self.place_at_grid(walker, 'C4', scale_factor=0.3)
        walker.move_to(number_line.number_to_point(0) + UP * 0.4)

        self.play(Create(number_line), Create(wall))
        self.play(FadeIn(walker))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Incremental movement representing Zeno's Paradox
        current_val = 0
        steps = [1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125]
        for step in steps:
            current_val += step
            self.play(walker.animate.move_to(number_line.number_to_point(current_val) + UP * 0.4), run_time=0.6)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The equation 1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 +... = 2 appears in light blue (#ADD8E6).
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        eq_conv = Text("1 + 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ... = 2", font_size=24, color=COLOR_CONV)
        # Fix Issue 33: Positioning complex label at B5.
        self.place_at_grid(eq_conv, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(eq_conv))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The Harmonic series 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 +... appears in red (#FF4500).
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        eq_div = Text("1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + ...", font_size=24, color=COLOR_DIV)
        self.place_at_grid(eq_div, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid['D5'] + RIGHT*1.5, end=self.grid['D6'] + RIGHT*1.5, color=COLOR_DIV)
        inf_label = Text("Infinity", font_size=20, color=COLOR_DIV).next_to(arrow, UP)
        
        self.play(Write(eq_div))
        self.play(Create(arrow), Write(inf_label))
        
        self.wait(3)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)
